purpose: Six-image comparison of cat-head integration directions, with required simple round-headed supporting character
common_prompt: Create a polished hand-drawn 2D story illustration in a horizontal 16:9 frame. Use Image 1 only to preserve the protagonist's identity. Show exactly two characters in the same quiet apartment corridor: the protagonist and the same supporting character. The protagonist is the same orange Scottish Fold cat-headed person, retaining the reference's compact round head, full cheeks, short muzzle, folded ears, large round dark eyes with a narrow amber rim, pink nose, cream muzzle, white whiskers, forehead M and orange tabby markings. He has a compact upright human body around 3 to 3.2 head-heights, very short neck, grey hoodie, black trousers, rounded cat-paw hands and bare cat-paw feet, no tail. The head, neck and hoodie collar must look intentionally connected, with the hood/collar supporting the base of the head; no floating head or pasted-on seam. The supporting character MUST be a very simple round-headed cartoon person, matching the established side-character design: one smooth round pale head, exactly two tiny dot eyes, one short simple line mouth, no detailed facial features; small white mitten/glove hands with no fingers; plain dark simple clothes made from a few flat shapes. Use a compact simple silhouette and the same dark grey-blue outline weight as the protagonist. Keep this figure deliberately minimal and secondary. Do not render the supporting character as an ordinary detailed human, portrait, realistic person, anime character or 3D figure; no hair strands, eyebrows, nose, detailed ears, skin texture, fingers or detailed anatomy. Both characters share clean 2D linework, restrained flat fills and hard-edged shadows. The apartment corridor has a clear doorway, wall lamp and quiet depth; cool-neutral muted palette with one warm lamp accent. No text, letters, numbers, logos, UI, watermark, extra people, photorealism, 3D rendering, plastic toy appearance, extra limbs or human fingers on the protagonist.

direction_prompts.01-balanced: Direction 1, balanced face treatment: preserve all recognizable face features and their proportions, but use a middle level of facial detail. Keep the cheek shape, eye spacing, folded ears, muzzle, pink nose and tabby pattern. Reduce only the finest fur strands to a few controlled illustrated strokes. Use one coherent outline and light direction across head and body; let the hood and collar cradle the short neck naturally.
direction_prompts.02-proportion: Direction 2, proportion bridge: preserve the face identity and markings in full, but make the head slightly smaller relative to the torso and make the shoulders modestly broader, while keeping the overall compact 3-to-3.2-head-height character proportion. Maintain the very short neck and have the hoodie collar support the head naturally. Do not shrink or redesign facial features.
direction_prompts.03-collar-body: Direction 3, collar and body bridge: keep the reference face details and current head scale. Connect the white chest bib visually to the pale hood opening and collar so the transition looks designed without turning the body into fur. Give the hoodie and sleeves a little more hand-drawn fold and tonal detail to meet the face halfway; keep them clearly 2D, restrained, and less detailed than the face.

scene_prompts.A-standing: Scene A: medium two-shot, eye-level three-quarter view. Both characters stand beside the same closed apartment door, side by side with a little space between them. The protagonist stands at frame left; the simple round-headed supporting character stands at frame right. Both look calmly toward the viewer, neutral posture, both figures visible from head to mid-thigh.
scene_prompts.B-gesture: Scene B: the same medium two-shot, eye-level three-quarter view, same apartment corridor, same door, same lighting and left-right staging. The protagonist stands at frame left and listens with a slight head turn. The same simple round-headed supporting character at frame right makes one small white-mitten hand gesture toward the closed doorway. Both figures are visible from head to mid-thigh; keep the gesture simple and readable.

acceptance.01-balanced__A-standing: PASS. The cat's face remains recognizable with moderately controlled fur detail; collar and outline treatment make the head-to-body transition feel deliberate.
acceptance.01-balanced__B-gesture: PASS. The same face treatment holds in the listening pose; the supporting character is a simple round head with dot eyes, a short line mouth and white mitten hands.
acceptance.02-proportion__A-standing: PASS as a proportion study. The head is smaller against the body, while the eye spacing, cheeks, muzzle, folded ears and markings remain readable. The face still has more detail than the clothes.
acceptance.02-proportion__B-gesture: PASS as a proportion study. The smaller head and slightly broader shoulders carry into the interaction pose; the supporting figure remains within the specified simple cartoon style.
acceptance.03-collar-body__A-standing: PASS as a collar/body bridge study. The hood opening frames the white bib, and added clothing folds narrow the detail gap; the head remains dominant.
acceptance.03-collar-body__B-gesture: PASS as a collar/body bridge study. Face identity and bib remain legible in profile; the extra fabric detail is restrained and the supporting figure keeps the required round-head design.
acceptance.supporting_character_all_images: PASS. All six images use the same minimal round-headed person with two dot eyes, one short line mouth, white mitten hands and plain dark clothes; no realistic human rendering appears.
acceptance.comparison: Direction 01 is the strongest middle ground in the contact sheet. Direction 02 is the clearest head-size test. Direction 03 explores clothing/collar integration but still makes the head visually dominant.

next_step: Use Direction 01 as the baseline for the next refinement, then adjust only the one feature the user selects from Direction 02 or 03. Do not change persistent style rules until the user picks a direction.
